t: Born Isaïe Tasumbu Tawosa to a Tetela family in the Kasaï, Lumumba worked as a postal clerk and beer salesman before leading the Mouvement National Congolais from 1958, a party that did not draw on a particular ethnic base.

He became prime minister in June 1960, but within days an army mutiny, a Belgian intervention and the secession of Katanga began the Congo Crisis, and President Kasa-Vubu dismissed him on 5 September.

Arrested by Mobutu's troops in December 1960 and executed in Katanga on 17 January 1961, he has been remembered above all as a martyr, a status that historians such as David Van Reybrouck say owes more to his death than to his political successes.
dyk: On 30 June 1960, Lumumba, who had not been scheduled to speak, answered King Baudouin's independence day speech with an impromptu address; Time magazine called it a "vicious attack".
ev: Born Isaïe Tasumbu Tawosa in Onalua, in the Kasaï province of the Belgian Congo
Helps found the Mouvement National Congolais and becomes its leader; attends the All-African Peoples' Conference in Accra in December
Arrested in late October for inciting an anti-colonial riot in Stanleyville in which 30 people were killed, and sentenced to six months in prison
Independence is declared on 30 June; Lumumba, prime minister since the vote of 23 and 24 June, gives his impromptu speech, and the army mutiny of July opens the Congo Crisis
Kasa-Vubu dismisses him on 5 September; Mobutu announces a coup on 14 September; Mobutu's troops arrest Lumumba at the Sankuru River on 1 December
Flown to Katanga on 17 January and shot that night; his body is later dug up and dissolved in acid
His remaining tooth is handed to his family in Brussels on 20 June, and he is buried in Kinshasa on 30 June

f.born: 2 July 1925 as Isaïe Tasumbu Tawosa, in Onalua, Katakokombe region, Kasaï province, Belgian Congo; a Tetela, known in that group as Élias Okit'Asombo; son of Julienne Wamato Lomendja and François Tolenga Otetshima, a farmer
f.died: 17 January 1961 near Elisabethville in Katanga, shot by firing squads; his body was dug up and later dissolved in acid
f.role: Leader of the Congolese National Movement (MNC) from 1958 until his death; first prime minister of the First Congolese Republic, June to September 1960
f.known: the Congolese independence movement; the MNC; his independence day speech of 30 June 1960; the Congo Crisis; his dismissal by Kasa-Vubu and arrest after Mobutu's coup; his execution in Katanga; Lumumbisme
